root_cause: Console._write_buffer runs after every print (print -> _exit_buffer -> _check_buffer -> _write_buffer). With record=True it did _record_buffer.extend(self._buffer[:]) unconditionally, but inside capture() (_buffer_index > 0) the buffer is never flushed or cleared, so each print re-appended the whole accumulated capture buffer to the record: 'Print 1', 'Print 1 Print 2', ... quadratic duplication. Captured output is also never actually written to the terminal, yet it was being recorded.
best_solution: In Console._write_buffer change `if self.record:` to `if self.record and not self._buffer_index:` so segments are recorded only at the moment the buffer is really flushed to the output (buffer depth 0). Nested `with console:` contexts still get recorded exactly once when they unwind to depth 0; capture() content is never recorded because end_capture() deletes the buffer before _exit_buffer runs. Reasoning from the statement: repro the issue snippet, see duplicated lines in export_text(), notice record-extend sits outside the `if self._buffer_index == 0` flush guard, move it under the same guard.
acceptable_alternatives: Moving the `_record_buffer.extend(...)` line inside the existing `if self._buffer_index == 0:` block (equivalent). Any fix that records captured content once (e.g. recording in end_capture) fails, because the hidden test requires export_text() == 'Print 0\n' (captured prints excluded from the recording).

our_outcome_summary:
Failed in all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4 (74s, 55 calls) and v6 (126s, 101 calls) submitted only new repro scripts (reproduce_issue.py / repro_fix.py) with no change to rich/console.py; both repro scripts also asserted the WRONG semantics (captured text should appear in export_text), mirroring the old test. v7 produced an empty patch. v8 edited the wrong place: loosened the `assert self.record` guards in export_text/export_html to `self.record or self._record_buffer`, which does nothing for the duplication. Test log shows export_text() == 'Print 0
Print 1
Print 1
Print 2
...' unchanged.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is just 'Fix <X>' plus an issue link, reconstruct the bug by running a minimal repro that exercises the two named features together and print the actual output before editing; then look for a side effect (append/extend/record/log) that sits outside the guard that controls the real flush/commit, and move it under that guard. Do not treat the existing test of the same name as the spec when it encodes the buggy behavior, and never submit a patch that only adds a repro script without touching library source.
